entities.summary: Charles-Joseph, comte Bresson was a French diplomat who played a crucial role in the development of European diplomacy during the early 19th century. Born into a noble family, Bresson was educated at the École des Hautes Études Commerciales and began his career in diplomacy in 1820. He served as a diplomat in various European courts, including the French court, where he gained valuable experience in international relations. Bresson's diplomatic career was marked by his ability to navigate complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers. He was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of 1815, which ended the Napoleonic Wars and established the balance of power in Europe. Bresson's legacy extends beyond his diplomatic career, as he played a key role in shaping the development of modern diplomatic practices. He was a strong advocate for the principles of neutrality and non-intervention, and his work laid the groundwork for the development of modern diplomacy. In 1847, Bresson died, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most important diplomats of his time. His contributions to the field of diplomacy continue to be studied and respected by scholars and diplomats around the world. As he once said, 'Diplomacy is the art of saying 'no' without ever saying 'no',', which encapsulates his approach to international relations. Bresson's impact on European diplomacy cannot be overstated, and his work remains a testament to the power of diplomacy in shaping the course of human history.
